content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "This judge text resolves a link collision by declaring the point open, so it is the kind of chain-vs-chain decision the rule governs.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "I interpreted 'without naming whose body is the channel' under the rule's 'weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse': either it is a footing-based chain comparison after considering both chains, or it is the retired requirement that a verse explicitly state the contrary/naming; I read it as the latter.", "why": "The judge made the text's failure to name the channel decisive, so the collision was decided by absence of an explicit verse statement rather than by weighing the chains' footings."}
